🇺🇸 A CIVIL WAR SOLDIER'S GOLD COIN, FOUND IN A TEXAS CLOSET

During an estate evaluation in Buda, Texas, a green milk crate was found in a bedroom closet. Inside were an old cigar box and two shoe boxes.

The cigar box held an 1867-S $5 gold piece from the San Francisco Mint, with other coins of the period. The family believes they started with a great-grandfather, a Union soldier in the Civil War, and were passed down for generations.

Graded MS63 by PCGS, it is the finest known 1867-S half eagle. Fewer than 100 are believed to survive in any grade.

In October 2026, Heritage Auctions sold it for $97,600, more than four times the previous record of $22,800.

⚠️ "SILVER THURSDAY": THE DAY THE HUNT BROTHERS' SILVER BET BROKE

In the late 1970s, Texas oil heirs Nelson Bunker Hunt and William Herbert Hunt piled up silver. By the end of 1979, the brothers and a related company controlled about 195 million troy ounces.

Silver traded below $10 an ounce before August 1979. By January 1980 it topped $50. Then the exchanges tightened margin rules, and the price turned.

On Thursday, March 27, 1980, the Hunts could no longer meet their margin calls. Silver closed at $10.80. A group of 13 banks later arranged a $1.1 billion loan to a Hunt family company.

As 1980 showed, silver can move fast in both directions.
